defects_closed.title: the vscode namespace was overwritten, and the command bindings were never released
defects_closed.cause: bindVSCodeAPI created its own vscode object, ran the binders, and then wrote that empty object back over the global, discarding the object the binders had populated. Separately, each command binding holds a DUP'd callback that was never freed, so the runtime's GC list was not empty at JS_FreeRuntime.
defects_closed.symptom_before: typeof vscode.commands was undefined, so no extension could register a command; the runtime also aborted at teardown with 'list_empty(&rt->gc_obj_list)'
defects_closed.fix: publish the shared object before the binders run and never write it back; release the bindings while their context is still alive, at unload and at shutdown; make the trampoline refuse a released binding
defects_closed.verification: typeof vscode.commands.registerCommand is now 'function'; the command registers and executes; the process exits cleanly

defects_closed.title: registerCommand promised a Disposable that unregisters the command, and did not
defects_closed.cause: the registry had no removal path, so an unloaded extension left a command behind that dispatched into a context that no longer existed
defects_closed.fix: added VSCodeExtensionAPI::removeCommand, called it from the JS disposable and from unloadExtension
defects_closed.verification: the command count returns to its baseline when an extension is unloaded

defects_open.title: only the first extension loaded in a process registers a command
defects_open.symptom: loading and activating a second extension leaves the shared command count unchanged, and the second extension's command is not found by executeCommand
defects_open.evidence: the binding IS present in the second extension's own context (a probe in that context reports typeof vscode.commands.registerCommand = function), and the command count is 19 -> 19 across the load, so the call never reaches the registry
what_is_not_the_cause: the namespace binding: the probe shows registerCommand is a function in the second extension's context
the ownership contract: the probe proves the host's bind pattern is sound over 5000 cycles
a test artifact: the extension name, the entry file name and the extension id are all distinct for each test extension, and the id is now selected by name rather than by position
defects_open.likely_area: the extension's entry module is not evaluated for the second extension, or its evaluation is swallowed before the registerCommand call; the module identity the host uses for the cached module is the thing to compare next
defects_open.status: OPEN - reported, not claimed as fixed
